ArcadeCatchRound.description: catch — the answers rain down and one of them is right.
ArcadeCatchRound.title: ArcadeCatchRound

ArcadeLineRound.description:
defend the number line — where does this value sit, within a tolerance a finger can hit.

The gate holds ``tolerance`` under a quarter of the line: a tolerance that swallows the line
means no tap can be wrong, which is the exact failure the wave 30 judges scored 1.12 for.
ArcadeLineRound.title: ArcadeLineRound

ArcadeMatchRound.description: match pairs — two to six pairs, laid out shuffled.
ArcadeMatchRound.title: ArcadeMatchRound

ArcadeQuizRound.description: the running quiz with lives — the answer must be among the options, or no tap can win.
ArcadeQuizRound.title: ArcadeQuizRound

ArcadeSequenceRound.description: build the sequence — ``steps`` in their right order, plus any step that does not belong.
ArcadeSequenceRound.title: ArcadeSequenceRound

ArcadeSortRound.description: sort against the clock — ``order`` is the CORRECT order; the client shuffles it.
ArcadeSortRound.title: ArcadeSortRound

ArcadeSpec.description:
One bonus level: a side door in the middle of a chapter, never in the path.

``seconds`` is the clock where the mechanic has one. Catch falls at its own pace and the
sequence teaches rather than races, so neither carries it.
ArcadeSpec.title: ArcadeSpec

BranchInteraction.description:
Branch on the answer: a wrong choice routes to the beat that repairs it. §2's
discrimination row, and the only recognition primitive in the vocabulary.
BranchInteraction.title: BranchInteraction

BranchOption.description: One answer. A wrong one must be a REAL misconception and must say what it teaches.
BranchOption.title: BranchOption

CanvasMarkInteraction.description:
Mark the stage itself: a point, a line, a circle, a path. The learner draws the answer
rather than choosing it, and the drawing is checked against targets, never rendered as code.
CanvasMarkInteraction.title: CanvasMarkInteraction

CanvasTarget.description: A place on the stage a mark must land, with the finger's radius around it.
CanvasTarget.title: CanvasTarget

Card.description: One teaching card. Owned fields are strict; rich activities pass through verbatim.
Card.title: Card

CourseSpec.description: engine.compose output — the primary card-spec contract.
CourseSpec.title: CourseSpec

DiscoverySpec.description: A card's embedded guided-discovery: 1..6 stages, one idea each.
DiscoverySpec.title: DiscoverySpec

DropInteraction.description: Drop each token into the bin its rule admits. The classification row of §2.
DropInteraction.title: DropInteraction

DropToken.description:
A thing the learner picks up. ``why`` is the reason it belongs where it belongs — the
wrong-drop line is written from it, so a wrong drop teaches the idea rather than the game.
DropToken.title: DropToken

DropZone.description:
A bin with a rule.

The rule, in its simplest honest form, is ``accepts``: the tokens this zone is for. A token
outside it is refused with this zone's own ``feedback`` — "a third is a smaller share than a
half", not "wrong". ``capacity`` caps a zone that must hold exactly n.
DropZone.title: DropZone

Feedback.description:
What a move teaches. Every primitive carries one.

``wrong`` is the load-bearing half: it must say something about the concept ("a third is a
smaller share than a half"), never about the game ("try again"). The gate reads it.
Feedback.title: Feedback

HitBox.description: A touchable rectangle on the stage, never smaller than a finger and never off the edge.
HitBox.title: HitBox

ImageSpec.description: Marks a card whose visual is organic/complex — hydrated through the raster seam.
ImageSpec.title: ImageSpec

Interaction.description: The single act a card asks for before it reveals anything.
Interaction.title: Interaction

InteractionDesign.description:
The model's design for one concept's interaction — a composition, never code.

``source`` says whether the model wrote it or the template floor of §2 took over after two
refusals. ``refreshDays`` is the cadence a superadmin sets (ninety by default); a change to
the concept core supersedes it at once, which is what ``coreVersion`` is for.
InteractionDesign.title: InteractionDesign

InteractionStep.description: One beat of a design: a primitive, what it is for, and the surprise it lands.
InteractionStep.title: InteractionStep

Item.description: A workbook / boss recall item with a structurally verified answer.
Item.title: Item

Mark.description: One shape on a discovery stage's reactive canvas (0..100 by 0..62).
Mark.title: Mark

MatchInteraction.description:
Join each left to its right. The correspondence row of §2.

``card`` is the size of ONE card; the client lays two columns of that size out, which is how
a finger's law is expressed for a layout the spec does not place by hand.
MatchInteraction.title: MatchInteraction

RevealSpec.description:
The moment: what the learner sees that they did not before. ``what`` is that sentence and
``marks`` are the stage's own marks that light when it happens.
RevealSpec.title: RevealSpec

ScoreSpec.description: A score over a beat. ``perWrong`` is zero or negative: a wrong move costs, never pays.
ScoreSpec.title: ScoreSpec

SequenceInteraction.description:
Build it step by step, with a check at each step. The construction row of §2.

Not a sort: a sort ranks a set that is already on the table, a sequence makes the next thing
only once the last one holds.
SequenceInteraction.title: SequenceInteraction

SequenceStep.description: One step of a construction, and the check that opens the next one.
SequenceStep.title: SequenceStep

SimSpec.description: engine.simulate output — every formula CAS-verified before it lands here.
SimSpec.title: SimSpec

SortInteraction.description: Put a set into its order, all at once. The ordering row of §2.
SortInteraction.title: SortInteraction

SortItem.description: One card in an ordering, with its true place and why it sits there.
SortItem.title: SortItem

TimerSpec.description: A clock over a beat. A modifier, not an act: it never stands alone in a design.
TimerSpec.title: TimerSpec

VideoSpec.description: engine.video output. ``narrationAudio`` is null at verify; per-scene audio attaches live.
VideoSpec.title: VideoSpec
